rejected_detail.title: Test and demo counts in the new PR body do not reconcile with the body it replaces
rejected_detail.reason: _pr_body.md is a per-PR scratch file (git history: rewritten each PR); the replaced body was a prior PR's content at an older point in history — no reconciliation owed between successive PR bodies.

findings.title: Hover inspect card is never clamped to the viewport or tray band — traceability numbers render off-screen for map-edge nodes
findings.evidence: x := i32(anchor.x) + i32(s * 0.7); y := i32(anchor.y) + i32(s * 0.5); rl.DrawRectangle(x, y, NODE_HEALTH_CARD_W, NODE_HEALTH_CARD_H, card) — no clamp. Verified geometry: at the 1280×720 design grid view_compute gives scale=0.923, off_y=0, so a bottom-row node (row 29, screen y≈696) anchors the 52px card at y 708..760 — BOTH text lines (y+26, y+42) land below 720, fully invisible; a right-column node clips 64.8px. The repo's entity-anchored-panel convention (app/render/popover.odin:39-63, popover_rect) flips left / clamps into the viewport / stays clear of TRAY_CLEAR(46) precisely because nodes sit anywhere on the map.
findings.detail: Hard req 2 says a 🔴 node is ALWAYS traceable; the card is the traceability surface, and growth-born drowning nodes live exactly at the map periphery where the card is unreadable. Violates the established popover clamp convention.
findings.recommended_fix: Clamp/flip the card rect like popover_rect (flip left when x+232 > win_w, clamp y into [8, win_h - TRAY_CLEAR - 52]).

findings.title: Stuck-pile measurement implemented twice — warning_evaluate's inline nload loop vs node_health_measure; equality held only by a single-fixture test
findings.evidence: Both sites filter flow.packets identically (skip delivered/on_edge, skip waiting_ticks==0, sum packet_bandwidth per at_node) then strain_level(load*100/throughput, 70/90). view.odin:344 claims "the two arrays are equal by construction"; the pin (test_node_health_coherent_with_node_strain) runs ONE static fixture (node_health_fixture) for 120 ticks — no transition/demolish/multi-fixture case.
findings.detail: Any semantic edit (waiting_ticks rule, bandwidth, throughput) is now a two-site edit; the render telegraph swap's pixel safety and health/strain coherence rest on a fixture-scoped test, not shared construction.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract one shared per-slot stuck-load helper consumed by both warning_evaluate's node pass and node_health_measure — one implementation, two consumers; the never-serialized node_health separation is unchanged.

findings.title: The '@t400 host resolution' claim is false — the golden shows the host still RED at t400, and no test or golden actually pins a downward (resolution) transition
findings.evidence: PR body: "the host resolution + growth persistence @t400"; story card: "host resolution @t400". The demo's own comment: "tick 400 (20s): the host pile (pool-capped) red + growth content_hosts red... The host pipe draw lands this tick (the recovery begins in the T1 tail)". Ground truth verified by inspecting goldens/node_health/20000ms.png: the content_host shows a RED ring at the capture. node_health_test.odin pins only up-transitions (75%→Amber, 150%→Red); no core test resolves a pile (Red→None).
findings.detail: The pinned golden's documented contract is wrong: the capture shows red, not resolution. The downward transition — the recovery arc the story's launchable increment promises — is unpinned anywhere.
findings.recommended_fix: Correct the copy to "recovery begins @t400 (host still red in the capture)" or add a capture past the pile drain + a core test that draws the pipe and asserts the host clears to None.

findings.title: Dead/demolished slot → .None branch of node_health_evaluate has no test (4.1's twin branch has one)
findings.evidence: node_health_evaluate: `if !t.node_alive[ns] { cr.node_health[ns] = .None; continue }`. node_health_test.odin never demolishes a node (no demolish_node call). warnings_test.odin:449-479 (test_warning_dead_node_silent) pins the 4.1 twin branch (demolished node's slot reads None, no phantom events).
findings.detail: The demolish-a-drowning-node recovery path leaves a stale ring if the dead-slot branch regresses; 4.1 has the pin, 5.2 doesn't.
findings.recommended_fix: Mirror test_warning_dead_node_silent: demolish a red node, assert node_health[slot] == .None on the next tick.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.evidence: P0 100% (up-transitions + 70/90 ladder incl. 69/70/89/90/91 boundary pins, determinism, derive-don't-record negative control all green: 183 core tests, 29/29 demos, 204 drift mutations). P1 ≈86% — gaps: downward/resolution transition unpinned (W3), dead-slot branch untested (W4).
findings.detail: P0 100%, P1 80–89%, overall ≥80% → CONCERNS band: core correctness is pinned; the recovery/teardown half of the surface is not.
findings.recommended_fix: Close W3/W4 (resolution test + dead-slot test) to lift P1 to ≥90%.

findings.title: PR body overstates the replay pin: "live == replay levels at every tick" — the test compares only the final-tick levels snapshot (per-tick equality is hash-implied, not directly compared)
findings.evidence: live_levels := node_health_snapshot(&live) is taken ONCE after record_run(&live, 120, cat); per-tick only the serialized-state hashes are compared. The claim "levels at every tick" describes what the hashes imply, not what is directly asserted.
findings.detail: The pin is final-levels + per-tick hashes; per-tick level equality is inferred (pure function of identical serialized state), not directly compared.
findings.recommended_fix: Snapshot levels inside the stepped loop, or soften the body to "hash-identical at every tick; levels compared at the final tick".

findings.title: node_health_evaluate is O(nodes × packets) — measure rescans the full packet array per slot
findings.evidence: for ns in 0..<len(t.node_alive) { _, _, pct := node_health_measure(...) } — each call scans all flow.packets. (warning_evaluate's own accumulation is also O(packets×nodes), so the class matches the existing idiom; the new pass doubles the constant per tick.)
findings.detail: Cost multiplies with 5.1 growth + long runs; matches the existing 4.1 complexity class but doubles per-tick packet scanning.
findings.recommended_fix: Single pass over flow.packets accumulating per-node stuck units into a scratch array, then map slots to levels (this falls out naturally from the W2 shared helper).

findings.title: Input sampling + world picking inside draw_hud instead of handle_input
findings.evidence: draw_hud reads rl.GetMouseX/Y + runs snap_node picking; the codebase's only other mouse reads are main.odin:526 (handle_input) and :939 (mouse_tile helper); other draw-pass affordances (draw_demolish_popover) read stored app.sel_node/sel_pipe state.
findings.detail: Hover target is interaction state computed in the draw pass, deviating from the handle_input → App state → draw convention; a draw-pass-only hover is unreachable to 5.4's input-parity layer. Harmless today (read-only, presentation-only — the PR body scopes it as such).
findings.recommended_fix: Resolve the hovered node in handle_input into App state (e.g. app.hover_node, same guards); draw_hud only renders from it.

findings.title: State glyph/color vocabulary duplicated between the ring and the inspect card
findings.evidence: draw_health_ring maps Amber→state_strain+"!" / Red→state_critical+"!!" inline; node_health_card_state reimplements the same mapping (name + color + glyph) for the card.
findings.detail: Two render sites now encode the tri-state vocabulary; a future state or glyph change is a two-site edit.
findings.recommended_fix: Share one state→(color, glyph) mapping proc in the render package; the ring and card both consume it.

findings.title: Hover card draws over the demolish popover's button while the cursor is within snap radius of the selected node
findings.location: app/main.odin:1215-1226 (draw order: popover at :350, draw_hud at :387)
findings.evidence: The demolish popover is drawn at main.odin:350, draw_hud (with the hover card, near-opaque alpha 240) at :387 — the card wins z-order. Geometry: popover spans anchor.y-20..+72 (h=92); card spans anchor.y+~12..+64; the demolish button (pop.y+h-36 → anchor.y+36..+82) is occluded by the card for anchor.y+36..+64. The hover guard has no sel_node check.
findings.detail: Selecting a junction (cursor on the node = inside snap radius) immediately paints the card over the demolish button until the cursor leaves. Hit-testing still works (geometric, not z-order) — visual occlusion only.
findings.recommended_fix: Skip the hover card while app.sel_node >= 0, or draw it before the popover pass.

findings.title: Card geometry comment says "2-line card" but the card draws three text rows (and the trace line's 12px text ends 2px past the 52px frame)
findings.evidence: Comment: "a small 2-line card: the state line + the traceability line"; the proc draws node_label (y+8), state name (y+26), trace (y+42) — three rows; trace text spans y+42..y+54 vs card bottom y+52.
findings.detail: Comment/geometry drift on a fixed-size card; the trace line's descenders touch/cross the bottom border.
findings.recommended_fix: Update the comment to three rows; nudge card height to 56 or the trace line to y+38.

findings.title: Hover inspect card render (P2 app surface) has no automated pin — sanctioned by the app-layer-only convention
findings.evidence: No @(test) or golden references draw_node_health_card; the harness capture path never calls draw_hud (verified: draw_hud is called only from app/main.odin:387). The PR body documents this as the golden-stability contract (5.3 chip precedent), and the numbers the card renders are pinned in core.
findings.detail: Layout/state-name mapping/hover gating are untested by design; core numbers are pinned. Informational.
findings.recommended_fix: None required (convention-sanctioned); the W1 clamp fix will likewise be visually verified.
